purpose: Compiler-discovered public SDK facts and finite owning callback closure; consumer explanations are authored in the documentation scripts. Not content acceptance.

discoveryScope.entrypoints: All exports in the actual SDK package export map, including export-star and explicit overrides.
discoveryScope.parser: Installed TypeScript compiler with SDK tsconfig.build.json; JSON Schema recursive keyword extraction with explicit unsupported-keyword failures.

exclusions.surface: Internal types outside the public reachable closure
exclusions.reason: Not selected by this SDK contract boundary. All compiler-resolved reachable KubeClaw support declarations are inventoried separately without adding named exports; newly reached unsupported local source shapes fail explicitly.

exclusions.surface: Node, TypeScript and dependency implementation internals
exclusions.reason: Referenced types and relevant selected consumers are linked; SDK enumeration does not duplicate all upstream APIs.

discoveryScope.readerTask: Select an SDK entrypoint, follow its consumer meaning and exact field/codec rules, and use the bounded pure JSON example.

exports.name: AdapterActivationContext
exports.consumerSemantics: Adapter factory input. registration identifies the resolved package and registration; config is the validated adapter configuration. invoke and invokeConfidential use existing dependency grants. emit must use the plugin event namespace. Optional withCleanup provides one bounded cleanup phase, not extra permissions.
exports.example: const factory = (context: AdapterActivationContext) => ({ ready: async () => {}, invoke: async () => ({}), shutdown: async () => {} });

exports.name: AdapterActivationId
exports.consumerSemantics: Historical adapter activation owner token. It contains the package and registration names, not a stage run ID. The schema limits each part and the whole token; do not invent a stage attempt from this string.

exports.name: AdapterCleanupContext

members.signature: invoke(capability: string, request: CapabilityInvocation, options?: AdapterDependencyOptions): Promise<Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>;
invokeConfidential(capability: string, request: CapabilityInvocation, options?: AdapterDependencyOptions): Promise<Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>;

exports.consumerSemantics: Cleanup receives its own AbortSignal and dependency invocation methods. The runtime requires a current invocation owned by the adapter before it enters cleanup. Lifecycle revocation and existing capability grants still apply.

exports.name: AdapterDependencyOptions
exports.consumerSemantics: Optional signal joins the lifecycle and parent signals. deliveryId is optional; when present, the runtime requires a nonblank string of at most 512 UTF-16 code units and a parent invocation. It does not create an observer delivery or grant permission.

exports.name: AdapterFactory
exports.consumerSemantics: Factory receives an activation context and returns an adapter, directly or through a Promise. The runtime starts required dependency adapters before this factory, then calls ready. A factory rejection stops startup and triggers rollback.
exports.example: const factory: AdapterFactory = context => ({ ready: async () => {}, invoke: async () => ({}), shutdown: async () => {} });

exports.name: AdapterInstance
exports.consumerSemantics: Implement ready, invoke and shutdown. Optional receipt looks up an earlier external result for an EffectRequest and may return undefined. An invoke Promise is not proof of durable completion: the effect coordinator owns receipts, locking and recovery. Honor the supplied abort signals.
exports.example: const instance: AdapterInstance = { ready: async () => {}, invoke: async ({signal}) => { signal.throwIfAborted(); return {}; }, shutdown: async () => {} };

exports.name: AdapterInvocation

members.signature: request: { [k: string]: any; } & { runtimeDispatchProfile?: RuntimeDispatchProfile; schemaVersion: "effect-request.v2"; effectId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: EffectIdempotencyKey; deliveryId?: EffectDeliveryId; attempt: EffectAttemptIdentity; capability: NamespacedId; operation: LocalId; resource: ResourceIdentity; payload: JsonObject; requestedAt: string; }

unionVariants.signature: FencedAdapterInvocation

members.name: request
members.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { runtimeDispatchProfile?: RuntimeDispatchProfile; schemaVersion: "effect-request.v2"; effectId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: EffectIdempotencyKey; deliveryId?: EffectDeliveryId; attempt: EffectAttemptIdentity; capability: NamespacedId; operation: LocalId; resource: ResourceIdentity; payload: JsonObject; requestedAt: string; }

unionVariants.signature: ConfidentialAdapterInvocation

members.name: request
members.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { runtimeDispatchProfile?: RuntimeDispatchProfile; schemaVersion: "effect-request.v2"; effectId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: EffectIdempotencyKey; deliveryId?: EffectDeliveryId; attempt: EffectAttemptIdentity; capability: NamespacedId; operation: LocalId; resource: ResourceIdentity; payload: JsonObject; requestedAt: string; }

exports.consumerSemantics: Discriminated union. confidential: true excludes lock and fence. Otherwise lock and fence are required and confidential may be absent or false. request carries the admitted effect and signal bounds cancellation. The reachable fence and variant interfaces are not named exports from the SDK entrypoint.

exports.name: AdapterLifecycle
exports.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { schemaVersion: "adapter-lifecycle.v2"; provider: RegistrationProvenance; status: "activating" | "ready" | "degraded" | "stopping" | "stopped" | "failed"; changedAt: string; reason?: Reason; }
exports.consumerSemantics: Records adapter startup, readiness, degradation and shutdown state with provider provenance and change time. degraded or failed requires a reason at schema validation. This record describes state; it does not start or stop an adapter.

exports.name: AdapterRegistration
exports.consumerSemantics: Manifest entry connects a module/export and config schema to provided and required capabilities. At least one provided capability is required; capability arrays must have unique items. Declaring a requirement is not the same as receiving a grant.

exports.name: AdministrativeReopenDecision
exports.signature: { schemaVersion: "administrative-reopen.v2"; decisionId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: OpaqueId; runId: OpaqueId; stageId: LocalId; actor: { type: "operator" | "administrator"; id: OpaqueId; }; reason: Reason; continuation: "remediation"; remediationStageId: LocalId; decidedAt: string; } | { schemaVersion: "administrative-reopen.v2"; decisionId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: OpaqueId; runId: OpaqueId; stageId: LocalId; actor: { type: "operator" | "administrator"; id: OpaqueId; }; reason: Reason; continuation: "retry" | "cancel"; packageUpgrades?: [{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }, ...{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }[]]; decidedAt: string; }

unionVariants.signature: { schemaVersion: "administrative-reopen.v2"; decisionId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: OpaqueId; runId: OpaqueId; stageId: LocalId; actor: { type: "operator" | "administrator"; id: OpaqueId; }; reason: Reason; continuation: "remediation"; remediationStageId: LocalId; decidedAt: string; }

{ schemaVersion: "administrative-reopen.v2"; decisionId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: OpaqueId; runId: OpaqueId; stageId: LocalId; actor: { type: "operator" | "administrator"; id: OpaqueId; }; reason: Reason; continuation: "retry" | "cancel"; packageUpgrades?: [{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }, ...{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }[]]; decidedAt: string; }

members.name: packageUpgrades
members.signature: [{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }, ...{ pluginId: NamespacedId; from: PackageIdentity; to: PackageIdentity; }[]]

exports.consumerSemantics: Administrative continuation record for a run and stage. remediation requires remediationStageId. retry or cancel may contain package upgrades. Actor is an operator or administrator. A well-typed record does not itself authorize or execute reopening.

exports.name: ArtifactRef
exports.consumerSemantics: Reference to exact stored bytes: artifactId, namespace, mediaType, digest, sizeBytes and producer belong together. Optional encoding selects portable JSON only when explicitly present. Absence preserves the historical producer bytes. A digest proves byte agreement, not producer authority or permission.

exports.name: AttemptIdentity
exports.consumerSemantics: Identifies one numbered stage attempt in a run. attemptNumber is an integer of at least one in the schema. Keep run, stage, attempt token and number together when comparing producer ownership.

exports.name: CURRENT_REVIEW_CACHE_PROFILE
exports.signature: { readonly schemaVersion: "review-cache-profile.v1"; readonly recordVersion: "review-content-cache.v2"; readonly encoding: "json-utf16-v1"; }

rule.description: Explicit immutable run-owned review cache producer profile. Historical absence preserves review-content-cache.v1 and its original effect operations.

exports.consumerSemantics: Frozen generated constant: review-cache-profile.v1, review-content-cache.v2 and json-utf16-v1. It selects the current cache producer only when the run context explicitly carries it. Artifact encoding, runtime transport and other digest versions do not imply this profile.

exports.name: CURRENT_RUNTIME_DISPATCH_PROFILE

rule.description: Explicit current runtime transport producer profile. Absence in historical contexts preserves the legacy producer; no profile is inferred from another digest version.

exports.consumerSemantics: Frozen generated constant: runtime-dispatch-profile.v1 with json-utf16-v1. Producers explicitly bind this run-owned transport choice; historical absence keeps the legacy producer. It is not inferred from a review cache or artifact version.

exports.name: CapabilityGrant
exports.consumerSemantics: A lease grant selects a capability, resolved provider and constraint object. Constraint meaning belongs to the capability authorization implementation. Possession of a TypeScript object is not a grant from the runtime.

exports.name: CapabilityInvocation
exports.consumerSemantics: Public named type is the readonly runtime interface, not the wider generated alias of the same name. Supply operation, resource.type, resource.canonicalId and payload. Optional runtimeDispatchProfile is control metadata; the owning schema restricts it to dispatch on runtime.agent. The helper that binds a profile does not itself enforce operation/resource rules; core validates the tagged request.

exports.name: DecisionFacts
exports.consumerSemantics: Stage decision facts use namespaced keys and scalar string, number, boolean or null values. A downstream activation condition refers to one fact and compares its value. Nested objects and arrays are outside the schema.

exports.name: EffectAttemptIdentity
exports.signature: AttemptIdentity | { runId: AdapterActivationId; stageId: "adapter-activation"; attemptId: AdapterActivationId; attemptNumber: 1; }

unionVariants.signature: AttemptIdentity
{ runId: AdapterActivationId; stageId: "adapter-activation"; attemptId: AdapterActivationId; attemptNumber: 1; }

rule.description: Exact historical adapter-activation producer domain. Core additionally checks equal runId and attemptId against the actual activation owner.

exports.consumerSemantics: Either a normal AttemptIdentity or the exact historical adapter activation shape. The latter has stageId adapter-activation and attemptNumber 1; core also checks that runId and attemptId name the actual activation owner. The union alone does not make those strings equal.

exports.name: EffectDeliveryId

rule.description: The original public adapter dependency delivery token: nonblank and at most 512 characters. Observer delivery contracts remain opaque IDs.

exports.consumerSemantics: Adapter dependency delivery token: schema maxLength is 512 Unicode code points; the runtime separately requires nonblank text of at most 512 UTF-16 code units. This is not the stricter observer delivery ID grammar. Runtime checks require a parent owner when a dependency call supplies it.

exports.name: EffectIdempotencyKey

rule.description: Existing opaque keys, plus the exact historical adapter dependency producer grammar. Package/capability names retain their 160-character bounds and registration its 96-character bound. New dependency keys are compact opaque IDs.

exports.consumerSemantics: Key used to detect a repeated effect request. The schema accepts compact opaque IDs and the exact historical adapter dependency key grammar. New dependency producers use compact opaque IDs. Reuse with different request identity or payload is a conflict, not permission to perform another effect.

exports.name: EffectJournal
exports.consumerSemantics: Persistence interface: record requested effects, atomically accept them with a boolean result, record completed receipts and look up requests/receipts by idempotencyKey. Missing lookups resolve to undefined. This interface supplies no storage backend, retention policy or universal retry safety.

exports.name: EffectReceipt
exports.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { schemaVersion: "effect-receipt.v2"; effectId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: EffectIdempotencyKey; adapter: PackageResolution; status: "accepted" | "completed" | "failed"; result?: JsonObject; error?: Reason; recordedAt: string; }
exports.consumerSemantics: Durable effect status and resolved adapter provenance. accepted has neither result nor error; failed requires error and forbids result; completed forbids error and may contain result. These conditional rules are in the schema even though the TypeScript interface allows optional members.

exports.name: EffectRequest
exports.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { runtimeDispatchProfile?: RuntimeDispatchProfile; schemaVersion: "effect-request.v2"; effectId: OpaqueId; idempotencyKey: EffectIdempotencyKey; deliveryId?: EffectDeliveryId; attempt: EffectAttemptIdentity; capability: NamespacedId; operation: LocalId; resource: ResourceIdentity; payload: JsonObject; requestedAt: string; }
exports.consumerSemantics: Admitted effect envelope binds idempotency, attempt, capability, operation, resource and payload with a request time. Optional deliveryId belongs to dependency identity. Tagged runtime dispatch restricts capability, operation and resource type. Do not manufacture a request to bypass lease admission or fencing.

exports.name: EventIdentity
exports.consumerSemantics: Run ID is required; stage, attempt, effect, wait and artifact IDs are optional links. Omission means the event does not carry that link. It does not mean that a missing value should be copied from an unrelated event.

exports.name: InvocationLease
exports.signature: { [k: string]: any; } & { schemaVersion: "invocation-lease.v2"; leaseId: OpaqueId; attempt: AttemptIdentity; registration: RegistrationProvenance; status: "active" | "revoked"; grants: CapabilityGrant[]; limits: { wallTimeMs: number; memoryBytes: number; cpuMillis: number; }; issuedAt: string; expiresAt: string; revokedAt?: string; revocationReason?: Reason; }
exports.consumerSemantics: Core-owned active or revoked invocation authority. Contains attempt, registration, grants, resource limits and issue/expiry times. Revoked leases require revokedAt and revocationReason in the schema. An active status string is not sufficient: runtime checks the current revocable lease before calls.

exports.name: JsonObject
exports.consumerSemantics: Generated open object shape. Arbitrary property values remain any in TypeScript; this does not guarantee the strict JSON value domain used by canonicalJson and portableJson. Validate at the owning boundary before serialization.

exports.name: LifecycleEvent
exports.consumerSemantics: Core lifecycle event with a closed event-type enum, sequence, identity, time, payload and nullable causationId. Sequence starts at one in the schema. null causation is allowed; omission is not. Observer code receives this or PluginDomainEvent, not an unversioned message.

exports.name: LocalId
exports.consumerSemantics: Local registration/stage identifier. Schema permits lowercase alphanumeric segments separated by dot, underscore or hyphen, at most 96 characters. Unlike NamespacedId, a separator is not required.

exports.name: NamespacedId
exports.consumerSemantics: Namespaced identifier such as a capability or stage type. The schema requires at least two lowercase alphanumeric segments separated by dot, underscore or hyphen, at most 160 characters. The TypeScript string alias does not enforce this.

exports.name: ObserverCheckpoint
exports.consumerSemantics: Observer progress record binds registration, run, sequence, event ID and update time. Sequence may be zero; eventId may be null but is required. The type does not persist or advance the checkpoint.

exports.name: ObserverDelivery
exports.consumerSemantics: One observer delivery attempt links observer provenance and a lifecycle or plugin event. attemptNumber is at least one. Observer handlers must account for at-least-once delivery; this envelope is not an exactly-once guarantee.

exports.name: ObserverHandler
exports.consumerSemantics: Async callback receives delivery and plugin invocation context and resolves with no result. A thrown or rejected error is an observer failure for the runtime policy. Use the context for granted effects; a callback does not create its own lease.
exports.example: const handler: ObserverHandler = async (delivery, context) => { const run = delivery.event.identity.runId; };

exports.name: ObserverRegistration
exports.consumerSemantics: Manifest callback entry declares subscriptions, at_least_once delivery, per_run ordering, failure mode and bounded attempts/backoff/timeout. At least one subscription is required. Checkpoint/config schemas and required capabilities are explicit; no failure policy default is declared here.

exports.name: OpaqueId
exports.consumerSemantics: Schema identifier begins with an ASCII letter or digit and then permits letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon and hyphen, to 192 characters total. Treat its meaning as owner-defined; do not parse a run or producer from arbitrary text.

exports.name: OptionalAbsenceReader
exports.consumerSemantics: Zero-argument value reader used by the selector helpers. Readers run in order until the selector accepts a value. Reader exceptions propagate; the alias provides no asynchronous waiting or exception suppression.

exports.name: PLUGIN_API_VERSION
exports.consumerSemantics: Literal pipeline-plugin-v2 token for the plugin manifest API version. It is not the package version, Node version, effect schema version or transport encoding.

exports.name: PORTABLE_JSON_ENCODING
exports.consumerSemantics: Exact artifact/source identity tag kubeclaw-json.utf16.v1. It differs from the profile encoding field json-utf16-v1. Select it explicitly for the owning contract; never attach it to historical bytes after the fact.

exports.name: PackageIdentity
exports.consumerSemantics: Immutable package identity includes plugin ID, pipeline-plugin-v2 API version, package version and content digest. Package version follows the schema version grammar. Identity records exact content; it does not assert a trust decision.

exports.name: PackageProvenance
exports.consumerSemantics: Resolved package source, canonical path and explicit trust evidence. Publisher attestation requires attestationDigest. trustScope is a recorded classification, not permission that plugin code can assign to itself. The registry, not this interface, resolves and verifies packages.

exports.name: PackageResolution
exports.consumerSemantics: Package identity plus registrationId selects the exact implementation surface. The same package may contain several registrations; preserve this field in provider/receipt ownership comparisons.

exports.name: PipelineDefinition
exports.consumerSemantics: Versioned pipeline definition requires an ID, positive maximum concurrency and a nonempty stage list. Individual dependencies, activation and retry settings belong to StageDefinition. The schema shape alone does not validate graph cycles or execute the pipeline.

exports.name: PluginContext
exports.consumerSemantics: Serialized invocation input contains the lease, resolved config, input and visible artifacts. Optional guidance/lifecycle fields carry caller information; their absence is permitted. Optional runtime and cache profiles are explicit independent producer selections. The runtime wraps this contract in PluginInvocationContext methods.

exports.name: PluginDomainEvent
exports.consumerSemantics: Plugin-produced event includes registration provenance and a plugin-prefixed type, unlike the core closed lifecycle enum. It retains required sequence, run identity, nullable causation and time. Runtime emission checks the plugin namespace and current run; typing the payload does not bypass those checks.

exports.name: PluginInvocationContext
exports.consumerSemantics: Runtime wrapper exposes contract, invoke, emit and artifact. Core checks the active lease on each call. invoke requires a grant and capability authorization; emit requires the plugin event namespace and same run. artifact returns a visible reference or undefined and can fail when the lease is inactive. No method grants arbitrary host access.

exports.name: PluginManifest
exports.signature: PluginManifest1 & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

unionVariants.signature: { [k: string]: any; stages: [any, ...any[]]; } & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

{ [k: string]: any; observers: [any, ...any[]]; } & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

{ [k: string]: any; adapters: [any, ...any[]]; } & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

{ [k: string]: any; testProviders: [any, ...any[]]; } & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

{ [k: string]: any; reportAdapters: [any, ...any[]]; } & { id: NamespacedId; apiVersion: "pipeline-plugin-v2"; packageVersion: string; stages: StageRegistration[]; observers: ObserverRegistration[]; adapters: AdapterRegistration[]; testProviders?: TestProviderRegistration[]; reportAdapters?: ReportAdapterRegistration[]; }

exports.consumerSemantics: Package manifest declares stages, observers and adapters as required arrays; testProviders/reportAdapters are optional. At least one of the five arrays must be nonempty. API version is pipeline-plugin-v2. The registry validates JSON, then resolves modules and referenced schemas; the type does not activate a package.

exports.name: PluginManifest1
exports.signature: { [k: string]: any; stages: [any, ...any[]]; } | { [k: string]: any; observers: [any, ...any[]]; } | { [k: string]: any; adapters: [any, ...any[]]; } | { [k: string]: any; testProviders: [any, ...any[]]; } | { [k: string]: any; reportAdapters: [any, ...any[]]; }

unionVariants.signature: { [k: string]: any; stages: [any, ...any[]]; }
{ [k: string]: any; observers: [any, ...any[]]; }
{ [k: string]: any; adapters: [any, ...any[]]; }
{ [k: string]: any; testProviders: [any, ...any[]]; }
{ [k: string]: any; reportAdapters: [any, ...any[]]; }

exports.consumerSemantics: Generated auxiliary union captures the manifest requirement that at least one registration array is nonempty. It is exported because the generated contracts entrypoint uses export star. Do not use it alone as a complete manifest; PluginManifest adds identity and required arrays.

exports.name: PluginStateEntry
exports.consumerSemantics: Versioned plugin state record links namespace, registration, entry type, sequence, idempotency key, time and payload. attempt may be omitted or null. entrySchemaVersion is optional. The shape does not define a persistence backend or removal schedule.

exports.name: PluginSystemV2
exports.consumerSemantics: Generated wrapper interface exposes optional contract examples for type generation. It is not a runnable plugin manifest or a runtime dispatcher. Its members refer to individual owning schema definitions; omission of all wrapper members does not create a usable package.

exports.name: RUNTIME_RESULT_FILE_MAX_BYTES
exports.consumerSemantics: 2048-byte UTF-8 path limit enforced by buildRuntimeAgentTask. It limits the result path string, not the result JSON size and not a filesystem allocation.

exports.name: Reason
exports.consumerSemantics: Structured reason requires a namespaced code. Optional message is 1–4096 characters and details is an object. Omitted message is permitted; callers must not assume every reason has user-facing prose.

exports.name: RegistrationProvenance
exports.consumerSemantics: Registration origin binds package provenance, surface and registration ID. Surface is one of stage, observer, adapter, test_provider or report_adapter. Keep it with lifecycle and state records; its schema does not verify the package evidence.

exports.name: RelativeModulePath
exports.consumerSemantics: Schema path must be relative, exclude parent path segments, end in mjs/mts/js/ts and have at most 512 characters. A matching string does not prove a regular file or containment after filesystem resolution; the registry checks module resolution.

exports.name: RelativeSchemaPath
exports.consumerSemantics: Schema path must be relative, exclude parent segments, end in json and have at most 512 characters. Registry owns reading/compiling the actual schema. The string type does not establish that a file exists or contains valid JSON Schema.

exports.name: ReportAdapterFunction
exports.consumerSemantics: Callback accepts report bytes/media type and limits, and returns counts/cases/findings plus required duration/truncation metadata, directly or asynchronously. It does not own adapter provenance or sourceArtifact fields; Buster adds those and validates the result. Rejection is a failed report adaptation, not a passing test.

exports.name: ReportAdapterInput
exports.consumerSemantics: Input has report-adapter-input.v1, media type, Uint8Array bytes and three count limits. The report runtime verifies source digest/size and allowed media type before adaptation. No filesystem path or capability context is part of this callback input.

exports.name: ReportAdapterLimits
exports.consumerSemantics: maximumCases, maximumFindings and maximumCaseFindings bound returned detail. This interface contains no default values or process/memory/time limits. Buster checks its wider runtime limits and rejects output arrays above these bounds.

exports.name: ReportAdapterOutput
exports.signature: Pick<ReportAdapterResultV1, "durationMs" | "casesTruncated" | "omittedCaseCount" | "findingsTruncated" | "omittedFindingCount"> & { readonly counts: ReportCountsV1; readonly cases: ReportCaseV1[]; readonly findings: FindingV1[]; }
exports.consumerSemantics: Counts, case list and finding list are required; duration and truncation metadata are required by the test-gate contract. This is the callback-owned subset, not the final provenance-bearing ReportAdapterResultV1. Buster adds adapter/source fields, validates the full contract and count limits.

exports.name: ReportAdapterRegistration
exports.consumerSemantics: Manifest report parser registration identifies format, positive contract version, module/export and 1–32 unique media types. It is distinct from a capability adapter registration. Registering it does not give an invoke context.

exports.name: ResourceIdentity

rule.description: Capability-owned resource names include URLs, absolute paths, dot and catalog keys. Capability implementations retain their own URL, path and authorization constraints.

exports.consumerSemantics: Capability-owned resource type and nonempty canonical ID. Canonical IDs can be URLs, absolute paths, dot or catalogue keys; this schema does not apply a universal path grammar. The selected capability implementation checks its own resource and authorization rules.

exports.name: ResourceLock
exports.consumerSemantics: Core lock record binds resource, owner lease/activation ID and positive fencingToken with state and expiry. A fence rejects operations whose lock is no longer current. The record alone does not acquire/renew a lock; check the invocation fence at the external-effect boundary.

exports.name: ResultBase
exports.consumerSemantics: Generated shared stage-result base shape requires version, outcome and artifact array; reason is optional at this base level. It is intentionally broader than the outcome-specific StageResult union and must not replace final stage result validation.

exports.name: ResumeSignal
exports.consumerSemantics: Versioned signal binds idempotency, wait ID, signal type, authorized issuer identity, time and payload. Matching the shape is not authorization; the runtime compares it to the selected wait and issuer before continuation.

exports.name: ReviewCacheProfile

rule.description: Explicit immutable run-owned review cache producer profile. Historical absence preserves review-content-cache.v1 and its original effect operations.

exports.consumerSemantics: Finite current cache producer contract. recordVersion is review-content-cache.v2 and encoding is json-utf16-v1. Historical absence retains review-content-cache.v1 and its original operations. No other encoding/profile/version selects it implicitly.

exports.name: ReviewSource
exports.consumerSemantics: Source selection binds project, absolute repository root, architecture ref and relative paths. For dense plain-JSON input, optional identityEncoding selects portable and omission selects legacy. The local parseReviewSource checks text/path bounds but is not strict validation of arbitrary unknown objects. Its entry describes limits for inherited fields, getters/proxies and sparse paths.

exports.name: ReviewSubject

members.signature: readonly files: readonly { readonly path: string; readonly mode: '100644' | '100755'; readonly content: string; readonly digest: string; readonly sizeBytes: number }[];

exports.consumerSemantics: Frozen review identity extends ReviewSource with current run, source/architecture revisions, input digest, ordered file content/mode/digest/size and subject digest. File bytes come from the architecture revision, not necessarily current HEAD. parse validates content binding; verify also checks current repository revisions.

exports.name: RuntimeDispatchProfile

rule.description: Explicit current runtime transport producer profile. Absence in historical contexts preserves the legacy producer; no profile is inferred from another digest version.

exports.consumerSemantics: Finite runtime transport contract with runtime-dispatch-profile.v1 and json-utf16-v1. Context absence preserves historical transport. It is not an artifact encoding token or a review-cache profile.

exports.name: RuntimeRunEdge
exports.consumerSemantics: Graph edge connects from/to node identifiers. Schema requires strings but does not impose LocalId grammar here or check that the nodes exist. Graph compilation owns that adjacent check.

exports.name: RuntimeRunGraph
exports.consumerSemantics: Frozen execution graph snapshot accepts v2 or v3, includes pipeline ID, positive concurrency, nodes, ordinary/remediation edges and digest. JsonObject nodes are not a fully validated node model in this SDK type. Snapshot verification belongs to the runtime.

exports.name: RuntimeRunSnapshot
exports.consumerSemantics: run-snapshot.v3 binds graph, registry, digest and required runtime dispatch profile. It has no review cache profile field in this schema. Do not interpret the snapshot version as selecting a cache encoding.

exports.name: RuntimeRunSnapshotV4
exports.consumerSemantics: run-snapshot.v4 requires both independent runtime dispatch and review cache profiles with graph, registry and digest. The version does not authorize deriving either from artifact encoding. Both explicit profiles must satisfy their finite contracts.

exports.name: RuntimeWorkspaceReference
exports.consumerSemantics: Git adapter-issued workspace record binds repository/workspace roots, path, branch, source revision and attempt owner under runtime-workspace.v1. parse checks shape and owner equality; runtime separately checks the protected owner record. A supplied object is not proof that the workspace belongs to the caller.

exports.name: SourceBinding
exports.consumerSemantics: Select a preflight stage and exact input digest, optionally a review stage. Optional identityEncoding selects the source identity codec and must agree with the preflight subject. This binding is selection data, not an approval artifact or capability grant.

exports.name: StageAttempt
exports.consumerSemantics: Core attempt state links identity, owner registration, stage type and lease with retry/remediation counters and timestamps. Status values: created/dispatched/completed/timed_out/cancelled. Optional finish/dispatch times are data, not timers. The shape alone does not establish successful stage outcome.

exports.name: StageDefinition
exports.consumerSemantics: Pipeline stage selection includes dependencies, config/input and execution budgets. Optional activation compares a source-stage fact; optional request_fix route chooses remediation. Required maxAttempts/timeout are positive; maxRemediationCycles permits zero. Optional technical retry/repair settings have schema limits; no SDK default is supplied.

exports.name: StageRegistration
exports.consumerSemantics: Manifest stage entry selects module/export and config/input/result schemas plus required capabilities. All listed members are required, including an empty capabilities array when none are needed. It is separate from a pipeline StageDefinition that selects type and execution budgets.

exports.name: StageResult
exports.signature: (ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "passed"; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; facts?: DecisionFacts; }) | (ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "retry" | "request_fix" | "blocked" | "failed" | "timed_out" | "cancelled"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; }) | (ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "wait" | "orchestrator_required"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; wait: WaitRequest; }) | (ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "rate_limited"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; retryAt: string; })

unionVariants.signature: ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "passed"; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; facts?: DecisionFacts; }
ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "retry" | "request_fix" | "blocked" | "failed" | "timed_out" | "cancelled"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; }
ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "wait" | "orchestrator_required"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; wait: WaitRequest; }
ResultBase & { schemaVersion: "stage-result.v2"; outcome: "rate_limited"; reason: Reason; artifacts: ArtifactRef[]; retryAt: string; }

exports.consumerSemantics: Outcome-specific stage result. passed allows facts without reason; retry/request_fix/blocked/failed/timed_out/cancelled requires reason; wait/orchestrator_required also requires wait; rate_limited requires retryAt. Artifact array is required in every variant and may be empty. Runtime handles continuation, not this type.

exports.name: TestContractId
exports.consumerSemantics: Provider contract/schema identifier has lowercase path-like characters and an @ suffix with a positive version number, at most 256 characters. This is distinct from namespaced capability and local registration ID grammars.

exports.name: TestEvidencePolicy
exports.consumerSemantics: Explicit evidence selections for pass, fail and error outcomes. Each required array may be empty, has at most 128 unique local IDs, and refers to provider evidence types. The SDK declares no default evidence list.

exports.name: TestProviderCapabilityRequest
exports.consumerSemantics: Provider dependency request includes operation, typed resource and payload but no runtimeDispatchProfile member. It does not grant a capability; the provider execution context owns the permitted call. This shape is distinct from plugin CapabilityInvocation.

exports.name: TestProviderExecutionContext
exports.consumerSemantics: Provider receives cancellation signal, mutable workspace root, log(stdout/stderr, text/bytes) and granted invoke with an optional call signal. Output logging is separate from ProviderResultV1. The local capability broker combines cancellation signals and returns failures; no unrestricted host access is part of the type.

exports.name: TestProviderFactory
exports.consumerSemantics: Factory receives ProviderInvocationV1 and returns TestProviderInstance directly or asynchronously. The invocation/result types belong to the separate pipeline-test-gate contract package; they are not named SDK exports. Factory failure is not a passing test.
exports.example: const factory: TestProviderFactory = invocation => ({execute: async (invocation, context) => result});

exports.name: TestProviderInstance
exports.consumerSemantics: execute receives the invocation plus execution context and returns ProviderResultV1. Optional cleanup receives the same argument shapes and returns void. Honor cancellation and use explicit cleanup for resources your provider owns; this interface guarantees no automatic rollback of external effects.

exports.name: TestProviderPort
exports.signature: { name: LocalId; kind: "value"; required: boolean; schemaId: TestContractId; } | { name: LocalId; kind: "artifact"; required: boolean; schemaId?: TestContractId; mediaTypes: [string, ...string[]]; }

unionVariants.signature: { name: LocalId; kind: "value"; required: boolean; schemaId: TestContractId; }
{ name: LocalId; kind: "artifact"; required: boolean; schemaId?: TestContractId; mediaTypes: [string, ...string[]]; }

exports.consumerSemantics: Value port requires schemaId; artifact port requires 1–32 unique media types and may omit schemaId. Both declare name and required. A required:false port can be absent at the consuming boundary; it is not a JavaScript default value.

exports.name: TestProviderRegistration
exports.consumerSemantics: Manifest provider/fixture entry declares contract, module/export/config, input/output ports, required capabilities, retrySafe, matrix fields, report formats, evidence types and explicit outcome evidence defaults. retrySafe is a declaration for the test engine, not a proof that every external operation can repeat.

exports.name: ValueRecord
exports.consumerSemantics: Permissive Record<string, any> used by objectRecord. It does not constrain JSON values, prototypes, property descriptors or capability payloads. Prefer the owning contract when a stronger shape is required.

exports.name: WaitRequest
exports.consumerSemantics: Versioned continuation wait names kind, signal type, authorized issuer and required expiry. expiresAt may be null for no declared expiry; omission is invalid. Optional request carries continuation data. This type does not install a timer or accept a resume signal.

exports.name: approvedSource
exports.signature: (context: PluginInvocationContext, expected?: SourceBinding): Promise<{ subject: ReviewSubject; sourceRevision: string; } | undefined>
exports.consumerSemantics: Resolve the source revision from visible same-run artifacts. With expected binding, require its preflight and optional selected review. Without it, absent report and approval returns undefined; an approval without a report fails. Passed reports with findings require report-bound human approval. Select the latest unique attempt per stage; reject competing stages or tied artifacts. Apply bound blueprint sync, then one unambiguous implementation lineage; reject cycles and forks. Reads artifacts but does not mutate Git or grant a general trust scope.

exports.name: arrayValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Return the input array by reference; for non-array values that native Array.isArray can classify, including null and undefined, return a new empty array. A revoked proxy throws TypeError during classification. No element validation or copy occurs. The generic type is a cast, not a runtime check.

exports.name: buildRuntimeAgentTask
exports.consumerSemantics: Build instruction text that describes its serialized input envelope as immutable; it also includes atomic result-file instructions. It does not freeze the supplied payload. resultFile is limited to 2048 UTF-8 bytes; longer paths throw RUNTIME_RESULT_FILE_PATH_TOO_LONG. Native JSON.stringify serializes the payload once: undefined/function/symbol object fields are omitted, their array elements become null, and nonfinite numbers become null. Enumerable getters and toJSON can execute and transform output; their exceptions propagate, as can cycles/BigInt errors. Use trusted, already-JSON data when executable object effects are not intended. This is not the strict portableJson domain. This helper neither writes the file nor validates path containment or the returned agent result.

exports.name: canonicalJson
exports.consumerSemantics: Legacy JSON codec sorts object keys with localeCompare. Preserve it for existing identities; its collation is locale-sensitive and must not be relabelled portable. Accepted values and rejection codes are the same as portableJson. It returns text, writes no file and does not hash.

exports.name: captureReviewSubject
exports.signature: (sourceInput: unknown, input: unknown, context: PluginInvocationContext): Promise<ReviewSubject>
exports.consumerSemantics: Parse and sort the source paths; freeze clean HEAD and the architecture reference through git.repository.read; read regular files at that architecture revision. Verify each response path, mode, digest and UTF-8 size. Bind the input digest and current run, then verify both frozen revisions again. Calls Git read capabilities; does not commit or write source. Any capability rejection propagates.
exports.example: const subject = await captureReviewSubject(source, input, context);

exports.name: objectRecord
exports.consumerSemantics: Return a truthy non-array object by reference when native Array.isArray can classify it; otherwise return a new empty object. Class instances, live proxies and accessor-bearing records can pass. A revoked proxy throws TypeError during classification. It is a permissive convenience cast, not strict JSON validation.

exports.name: parseReviewCacheProfile
exports.consumerSemantics: Compare the complete strict portable serialization to the one generated current cache profile. Return the generated frozen constant on equality; otherwise throw REVIEW_CACHE_PROFILE_INVALID. Extra/missing fields, null and unknown versions fail. Strict JSON failures can occur before the profile-specific error.

exports.name: parseReviewSource
exports.consumerSemantics: For dense plain-JSON input, check project ID, absolute repository root, architecture reference and 1–128 unique safe relative paths. Text fields are nonempty, at most 4096 UTF-16 code units and exclude NUL/CR/LF. Paths exclude absolute paths, backslashes and empty/dot/parent segments. Only an own identityEncoding is guarded and must be portable. Property reads can inherit values or execute getters/proxy traps; a truthy inherited encoding is copied into an own output field, including an unknown tag. Array.some skips holes: a single-hole paths array passes and copies to [undefined]. Return a new object with sorted copied paths and discard unrelated fields. This is a limited local parser, not strict unknown-input validation; no Git access occurs.

exports.name: parseReviewSubject
exports.consumerSemantics: Validate the source, current run ID, two 40- or 64-character lowercase hex revisions, input digest and ordered files. Every file must match a sorted source path, executable/regular Git mode, content hash and UTF-8 size. Recompute the unsigned subject digest with the selected identity codec. Return the original subject. No repository freshness check occurs here.

exports.name: parseRuntimeDispatchProfile
exports.consumerSemantics: Strict portable serialization must exactly match the generated current profile; return its frozen constant. Wrong shape/version throws RUNTIME_DISPATCH_PROFILE_INVALID; invalid JSON domain can throw a CANONICAL_JSON error first. This parser does not dispatch an agent.

exports.name: parseRuntimeWorkspace
exports.consumerSemantics: Require an object with exactly the seven declared enumerable string keys and runtime-workspace.v1. Require a 40/64 lowercase hex revision. Require nonempty path/branch strings to 4096 UTF-16 code units without controls. Compare owner using legacy canonical JSON. Return the original reference. It does not prove containment, branch existence or a protected owner-file record; runtime performs that adjacent check.

exports.name: parseSourceBinding
exports.consumerSemantics: Check enumerable own string keys against stageId, inputDigest, optional reviewStageId and optional identityEncoding; this does not reject hidden/symbol keys or inherited fields. Stage names must be nonempty strings; digest must have sha256 and 64 lowercase hex digits. An own identityEncoding must be the portable token. Inherited encodings are not guarded and the original reference retains them; inherited required fields can pass. Reads can execute getters/proxy traps, so use trusted dense plain-JSON input for the stated contract, not this parser as strict unknown-input validation. Omitted reviewStageId is allowed; a present undefined value also passes this local parser. Return the original binding. Throws SOURCE_PREFLIGHT_BINDING_INVALID for failed checks.

exports.name: portableJson
exports.consumerSemantics: Serialize strict JSON with object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, independently of locale. Accept null, strings, booleans, finite numbers, plain/null-prototype records and dense standard arrays of enumerable data properties. Reject undefined, functions, symbols, BigInt, nonfinite numbers, proxies, cycles, exotic prototypes, hidden/symbol/accessor properties and extra/sparse array entries. Error codes are listed in the JSON section. Shared noncyclic objects are allowed; negative zero becomes 0. No getters, toJSON or proxy traps execute.

exports.name: readBoundArtifact
exports.consumerSemantics: Require same-run producer, application/json media type and size at most 4 MiB; then invoke artifacts.read/get_json_bytes with the full reference. Verify exact byte/reference/value binding and repeat digest/size checks. Return response.value by cast, not a validated record schema. Byte agreement is not blanket producer trust; approval/preflight helpers impose their own selection rules.

exports.name: redactStructuredValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Build a bounded redacted value: sensitive object keys matching authorization/cookie/password/secret/token/api-key/credential become [redacted]. Keep at most 1000 array entries or object entries; truncate beyond depth 16 and strings after a 65536-UTF-16-code-unit prefix, followed by `[truncated]` (65547 output units). No comprehensive secret detection is promised. Object enumeration may execute getters/proxy traps; cyclic graphs terminate through the depth bound, not cycle identity detection.

exports.name: resolveImplementationRevisions
exports.signature: (sourceStageId: string, context: PluginInvocationContext): Promise<{ base: string; head: string; }>
exports.consumerSemantics: Select earliest and latest unique implementation attempts for the named stage in the current run. Read and verify both exact JSON artifacts; require ready_for_testing and a valid source revision. First headBefore must be a valid 40/64 lowercase hex revision. Return base/head; do not use ambient repository HEAD or compare lexical revisions. Calls artifacts.read and propagates failures.

exports.name: resolveSourceRevision
exports.signature: (input: { readonly revision?: string; readonly sourceStageId?: string; }, context: PluginInvocationContext): Promise<string>
exports.consumerSemantics: Supply exactly one of revision and sourceStageId. An explicit revision must be 40/64 lowercase hex. Otherwise select the latest unique matching implementation artifact attempt in the same run/stage and read its ready_for_testing revision. Empty candidate sets and tied attempts fail; no fallback to HEAD occurs. Explicit revision needs no capability call.

exports.name: reviewCacheProfileFromContext
exports.consumerSemantics: First validate strict portable JSON for the complete contract. If the own reviewCacheProfile key is absent, return undefined. If present, parse exactly the current profile. Present undefined is rejected by strict JSON, not treated as legacy absence; null or unknown profile also fails. No context mutation occurs.

exports.name: reviewIdentityDigest
exports.consumerSemantics: Guard only an own identityEncoding: an own different value, including undefined, throws REVIEW_IDENTITY_ENCODING_INVALID. Then ordinary property lookup selects portable JSON for the portable tag, including an inherited tag; an inherited unknown tag selects legacy canonical JSON. Dense plain-JSON input without the key selects legacy. Reads can execute getters/proxy traps. Does not add a version tag to the returned sha256 digest, mutate source or normalize historical identities.

exports.name: runtimeDispatchProfileFields
exports.signature: (request: object, capability?: string): Readonly<{ runtimeDispatchProfile?: RuntimeDispatchProfile; }>
exports.consumerSemantics: Validate strict portable JSON for the whole request. Missing own profile key returns a new empty object. Present profile with a provided capability other than runtime.dispatch throws RUNTIME_DISPATCH_PROFILE_CAPABILITY_INVALID; otherwise parse the profile and return only that metadata. An omitted capability does not check capability identity. Same-named nested payload/model fields are ordinary data.

exports.name: runtimeWorkspaceGeneration
exports.signature: (owner: AttemptIdentity, scope: Readonly<{ repositoryRoot: string; branch: string; }>): string
exports.consumerSemantics: Hash legacy canonical JSON of owner, repositoryRoot and branch, then remove sha256: from the result. Output is 64 hex characters. Does not create a workspace, validate those typed arguments or bind portable identity.

exports.name: runtimeWorkspaceOwnerFile
exports.consumerSemantics: Hash the supplied workspacePath UTF-8 bytes and return .kubeclaw-workspace-owners/<hex>.json. No path normalization, validation, read or write occurs. Different JavaScript strings can encode to identical UTF-8 bytes: distinct lone surrogates become the same replacement bytes. No universal textual uniqueness or hash-collision exclusion is promised.

exports.name: selectDefinedValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Run readers in order; return the first value other than undefined or null. The selector accepts false, zero and empty text. If none qualifies, return the last value; no readers returns undefined despite generic T. Exceptions propagate; readers after selection do not execute.

exports.name: selectPresentValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Return the first nonempty string from the values, or empty text when none matches. Whitespace-only strings are nonempty and accepted. Other types, null and undefined are skipped; this helper does not trim or execute readers.

exports.name: selectTruthyValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Run readers in order and return the first truthy value. False, zero, empty text, null, undefined and NaN are skipped. If all fail, return the last value; no readers returns undefined despite generic T. Exceptions propagate and later readers do not execute after selection.

exports.name: sha256Bytes
exports.consumerSemantics: Hash the exact Uint8Array bytes and return sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hex digits. No JSON codec, encoding tag or trust check is applied. Wrong runtime argument types can cause Node crypto errors; this is not an unknown-input validator.

exports.name: sha256Text
exports.consumerSemantics: Hash the supplied text with Node crypto default UTF-8 and return sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex digits. Does not canonicalize JSON or version the identity. Byte size elsewhere must use UTF-8, not JavaScript string length.

exports.name: sourcePreflight
exports.signature: (value: unknown, context: PluginInvocationContext): Promise<{ binding: SourceBinding; subject: ReviewSubject; contract: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; }>
exports.consumerSemantics: Parse binding, select the latest unique source-preflight artifact from its explicit stage and current run, then read exact bound bytes. Require source-preflight.v1 and passed. Validate the subject and match identityEncoding, inputDigest and digest of the returned contract. Return binding/subject/contract. No artifact or failed/mismatched artifact rejects; never use an unrelated ancestor as fallback.

exports.name: textValue
exports.consumerSemantics: Return a string unchanged; every other value becomes empty text. Empty input text remains empty. This helper does not trim, convert, parse or validate.

exports.name: verifiedArtifactJsonText
exports.consumerSemantics: Verify artifact-json-bytes.v1, original UTF-8 byte size and digest; parse original text, compare strict portable value serialization, and compare the complete returned reference with expected. Digest and size must also agree with that reference. An explicitly encoded artifact must use the portable tag and its original bytes must equal portable serialization. Untagged historical JSON is not recanonicalized. Return original text, not reserialized text. Errors distinguish bytes/value/reference/encoding mismatch; JSON.parse and strict JSON errors propagate. No capability call, producer authorization or schema validation occurs.

exports.name: verifyReviewSubject
exports.signature: (value: unknown, context: PluginInvocationContext, expectedSourceRevision?: string): Promise<ReviewSubject>
exports.consumerSemantics: Parse the subject for the current run, freeze clean HEAD and the architecture ref again, and compare with subject revisions. Optional expectedSourceRevision replaces only the expected current HEAD; architecture must still match. Throw REVIEW_SUBJECT_STALE on revision mismatch. Calls git.repository.read but performs no source mutation.

exports.name: withRuntimeDispatchProfile
exports.consumerSemantics: If profile is undefined, return the original request unchanged without validating it. Otherwise parse current profile and validate strict JSON of the request. Reject any existing own runtimeDispatchProfile key. Return a shallow frozen copy with the selected profile. It does not validate dispatch operation/resource or deeply freeze payload.

exports.name: assertNever
exports.consumerSemantics: Testing entrypoint only. Exhaustiveness helper accepts never and always throws Unexpected contract variant followed by JSON.stringify(value). It does not return or validate a runtime union. Serialization errors such as cyclic input or BigInt can occur before the intended error if typing is bypassed.

validation.consumerSemantics: Owning validation first applies the selected JSON Schema without default insertion or coercion. providerInvocation and providerResult have no extra semantic branch in checkPipelineTestGateContract. reportAdapterResult additionally requires outcome counts to sum to total and unique case IDs. Complete cases require zero omittedCaseCount, exact total length and exact outcome counts. Truncated cases require positive omittedCaseCount, listed plus omitted equal total, and listed outcomes no greater than exact counts. Report and case findingsTruncated must be true exactly when omittedFindingCount is positive. Buster supplies adapter/sourceArtifact provenance before this validation. Failure returns errors from checkPipelineTestGateContract; validatePipelineTestGateContract throws PipelineTestGateContractError. Shape acceptance does not authorize provider execution.

providerDetails.selection: Buster selects these extra rules for kubeclaw.playwright@1, or whenever providerDetails.schemaId is kubeclaw.e2e-result.v1. Other provider-specific details remain governed by their owning provider contract, not a universal E2E requirement.
providerDetails.consumerSemantics: Require the exact E2E schema ID and SHA-256 of the owning schema bytes, then validate values against that schema. Total must equal passed plus failed plus skipped plus unexecuted and the number of test cases. IDs must be unique; the number of cases with each status must equal its count. Failure throws TEST_PROVIDER_E2E_DETAILS_INVALID.

consumerValidation.consumerSemantics: After providerResult schema validation, Buster requires total = passed + failed + skipped, and a passed outcome cannot have failed > 0. Evidence IDs and file paths must each be unique; runner-log is reserved; evidence types must be registered. Report evidence IDs must be unique, report formats registered, and each report must refer to declared test-report evidence.

Before admission, native JSON.stringify output must fit the configured provider-result UTF-8 byte budget. Buster applies schema, counts, selected details, evidence and report checks before freezing a clone. Artifact outputs must refer to declared evidence IDs. These runtime checks do not run merely because a callback has the TypeScript signature.

rule.description: Explicit immutable run-owned review cache producer profile. Historical absence preserves review-content-cache.v1 and its original effect operations.
Explicit current runtime transport producer profile. Absence in historical contexts preserves the legacy producer; no profile is inferred from another digest version.

Existing opaque keys, plus the exact historical adapter dependency producer grammar. Package/capability names retain their 160-character bounds and registration its 96-character bound. New dependency keys are compact opaque IDs.
Capability-owned resource names include URLs, absolute paths, dot and catalog keys. Capability implementations retain their own URL, path and authorization constraints.
The original public adapter dependency delivery token: nonblank and at most 512 characters. Observer delivery contracts remain opaque IDs.
Exact historical adapter-activation producer domain. Core additionally checks equal runId and attemptId against the actual activation owner.
